output_list.reason: The 'transfer' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the balance of the caller is only slightly above the transfer amount, an overflow can occur, causing the caller's balance to be set to zero, and granting the recipient the caller's entire balance.

The 'transferFrom' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the caller's available allowance is only slightly above the transfer amount, an overflow can occur, causing the caller's allowance to be set to zero, and granting the recipient the caller's entire balance.

The 'approve' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When the caller's allowance is only slightly above the approve amount, an overflow can occur, causing the caller's allowance to be set to zero, and granting the spender the caller's entire balance.
The 'receiveApproval' function has a wrong logic. It calls a spender's function without verifying the spender's identity, allowing attackers to exploit it and cause unexpected token loss.
The 'HumanStandardToken' constructor has a typo in it, causing it to be uncallable in real world.
